answers.question: What are Tesla's automotive regulatory credits and how are they recognized (2022 10-K)?
answers.reference_answer: Tesla earns tradable credits under regulations on zero-emission vehicles, greenhouse gas, fuel economy and clean fuel, and sells them to other regulated entities who use them to meet emission standards. Sales are recognized in automotive regulatory credits revenue. This revenue is tied to Tesla's new vehicle production, sales and negotiated pricing; Tesla monetizes credits proactively as new vehicles are sold under standing arrangements with buyers, typically close to production and delivery or to regulatory changes affecting the credits.
key_points: Tesla earns tradable credits under ZEV, greenhouse gas, fuel economy and clean fuel regulations and sells them to other regulated entities.
Sales are recognized as automotive regulatory credits revenue.
Credits are monetized as vehicles are sold under standing arrangements, so the revenue follows vehicle production and sales.

claims.text: Tesla earns tradable credits in the operation of its automotive business under various regulations related to ZEVs, greenhouse gas, fuel economy and clean fuel, and sells these credits to other regulated entities who can use them to comply with emission standards and other regulatory requirements.
cited_passages: Automotive Regulatory Credits We earn tradable credits in the operation of our automotive business under various regulations related to ZEVs, greenhouse gas, fuel economy and clean fuel. We sell these credits to other regulated entities who can use the credits to comply with emission standards and other regulatory requirements. Payments for automotive regulatory credits are typically received at the point control transfers to the customer, or in accordance with payment terms customary to the business. We recognize revenue on the sale of automotive regulatory credits, which have negligible incremental costs associated with them, at the time control of the regulatory credits is transferred to the purchasing party. Deferred revenue related to sales of automotive regulatory credits was immaterial as of December 31, 2022 and 2021. Revenue recognized from the deferred revenue balance as of December 31, 2021 and 2020 was immaterial for the years ended December 31, 2022 and 2021. During the year ended December 31, 2022 , we had also recognized $ 288 million in revenue due to changes in regulation which entitled us to additional consideration for credits sold previously.

Automotive Regulatory Credits We earn tradable credits in the operation of our business under various regulations related to zero-emission vehicles (“ZEVs”), greenhouse gas, fuel economy and clean fuel. We sell these credits to other regulated entities who can use the credits to comply with emission standards and other regulatory requirements. Sales of these credits are recognized within automotive regulatory credits revenue in our consolidated financial statements included elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. 8 Energy Storage System Incentives and Policies While the regulatory regime for energy storage projects is still under development, there are various policies, incentives and financial mechanisms at the federal, state and local levels that support the adoption of energy storage. For example, energy storage systems that are charged using solar energy may be eligible for the solar energy-related U.S. federal tax credits described below. The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (“FERC”) has also taken steps to enable the participation of energy storage in wholesale energy markets. In addition, California and a number of other states have adopted procurement targets for energy storage, and behind-the-meter energy storage systems qualify for funding under the California Self Generation Incentive Program. Our customers primarily benefit directly under these programs. In certain instances our customers may transfer such credits to us as contract consideration. In such transactions, they are included as a component of energy generation and storage revenues in our consolidated financial statements included elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K.

answers.question: What does TSMC's 2024 annual report say about its Arizona expansion and U.S. CHIPS Act support?
answers.reference_answer: Construction of TSMC Arizona's first fab began in April 2021 and volume production started by the end of 2024; a second fab, announced in December 2022, is under construction, and a third was announced in April 2024. The U.S. Department of Commerce agreed to award TSMC Arizona up to US$6.6 billion in direct funding for its Phoenix fabs, and TSMC Arizona can draw down up to US$5 billion in government loans; TSMC gives an irrevocable, unconditional guarantee of TSMC Arizona's financial obligations to the Department of Commerce. In March 2025 TSMC announced plans for three more U.S. fabs, two advanced packaging facilities and an R&D center.
key_points: The first Arizona fab reached volume production by the end of 2024; a second is under construction and a third was announced.

answers.question: How does Texas Instruments describe its capital allocation approach and its outlook for capital expenditures in its 2023 10-K?
answers.reference_answer: Disciplined allocation of capital is the second element of TI's strategy to maximize free cash flow per share growth; it spans how TI selects R&D projects, develops new capabilities, invests in manufacturing capacity, approaches acquisitions and returns cash to its owners. From 2014 to 2023 it allocated $94 billion, the largest share to organic growth (R&D, sales and marketing, capital expenditures and working capital for inventory). It expects capital expenditures to stay higher than historical levels as it invests in manufacturing and technology as part of long-term capacity planning. The U.S. CHIPS and Science Act of August 2022 established a 25% investment tax credit for certain U.S. semiconductor manufacturing investments; TI expects to receive the cash benefit of that credit for qualifying capital expenditures and has applied for the Act's manufacturing grants.
key_points: Disciplined capital allocation is the second element of TI's strategy to maximize free cash flow per share growth.
Of $94 billion allocated over 2014-2023, the largest share went to organic growth; allocation also covers acquisitions and returning cash to owners.
Capex is expected to stay higher than historical levels to build manufacturing capacity.
TI expects the CHIPS Act's 25% investment tax credit on qualifying capex and has applied for manufacturing grants.

This spans how we select R&D projects, develop new capabilities like TI.com, invest in new manufacturing capacity or how we think about acquisitions and returning cash to our owners. Over a 10-year period from 2014 to 2023, we allocated $94 billion, which reinforces the importance of discipline in capital allocation. The largest allocation over this period was to drive organic growth, which includes investments in R&D, sales and marketing, capital expenditures and working capital for inventory. In this period, we allocated just over $15 billion to capital expenditures. Our increased capital expenditures are to support future revenue growth, which will be a greater component of free cash flow per share growth going forward. Beyond that, we also allocated capital to dividends and share repurchases. Dividends are designed to appeal to a broad set of investors, and share repurchases are made with the goal of the accretive capture of future free cash flow for long-term investors. Lastly, for inorganic growth, we allocate to acquisitions that meet our financial and strategic objectives.

answers.question: What does UPS's 2024 10-K say about its agreement with Amazon and the network changes it plans in response?
answers.reference_answer: Amazon accounted for 11.8% of UPS's 2024 consolidated revenues. In the first quarter of 2025 UPS reached an agreement in principle with Amazon that will reduce Amazon's volume by more than 50% by June 2026, and UPS is making business and operational changes to match its workforce to its activity and eliminate stranded costs; if it cannot reduce costs, its profitability could be materially impacted. A U.S. network reconfiguration, an expansion of its Network of the Future program, could close up to 10% of its buildings in 2025 and shrink its vehicle and aircraft fleets and workforce; UPS cannot yet estimate the total cost. It expects to partly offset those costs through Efficiency Reimagined initiatives, an end-to-end process redesign expected to yield about $1.0 billion in annualized savings starting in 2025.
key_points: Amazon was 11.8% of UPS's 2024 consolidated revenues.
Under an agreement in principle, Amazon's volume will fall by more than 50% by June 2026.
UPS is matching its workforce to activity and eliminating stranded costs; failure to cut costs could materially hurt profitability.
A U.S. network reconfiguration may close up to 10% of buildings in 2025, and its total cost cannot yet be estimated.
Efficiency Reimagined is expected to save about $1.0 billion a year, starting in 2025, partly offsetting the reconfiguration costs.

answers.question: What drove the changes in Walmart's gross profit rate and operating expense rate in fiscal 2025?

Operating expenses as a percentage of net sales rose 36 basis points, mainly from higher variable pay after exceeding planned performance, more marketing and higher depreciation.

The operating expense rate rose because of higher variable pay, marketing and depreciation.

answers.question: What did Apple disclose in its fiscal 2024 10-K about the European Commission's Digital Markets Act investigations, and what could the Commission do if it finds a violation?
answers.reference_answer: On March 25, 2024 the Commission opened two formal noncompliance investigations under the DMA: one under Article 5(4) on how developers may communicate and promote offers to users of App Store apps and conclude contracts with them, and one under Article 6(3) on default settings, uninstalling apps and a browser choice screen on iOS. On June 24, 2024 it issued preliminary findings that Apple's App Store rules breach the DMA and opened a third investigation into Apple's new contractual requirements for third-party developers and app marketplaces. If the Commission finds a violation it can issue a cease and desist order and impose fines of up to 10% of Apple's annual worldwide net sales, and its order would apply immediately during an appeal unless stayed. Apple says it believes it complies with the DMA.
key_points: Two formal noncompliance investigations were opened in March 2024: Article 5(4) (how developers communicate and promote offers and conclude contracts) and Article 6(3) (defaults, uninstallation and browser choice).
Preliminary findings in June 2024 said the App Store rules breach the DMA, and a third investigation into new contractual requirements was opened.
A violation can bring a cease and desist order and fines of up to 10% of annual worldwide net sales.
Apple believes it complies with the DMA.

claims.text: Apple disclosed that on March 25, 2024 the European Commission opened two formal DMA noncompliance investigations against it — one under Article 5(4) concerning how developers may communicate and promote offers and conclude contracts with end users for App Store-distributed apps, and one under Article 6(3) concerning default settings, app uninstallation and a browser choice screen on iOS — and that on June 24, 2024 the Commission issued preliminary findings alleging Apple's App Store rules breach the DMA and opened a third formal investigation into whether Apple's new contractual requirements for third-party developers and app marketplaces may violate the DMA. If the Commission makes a final determination of a violation, it can issue a cease and desist order and may impose fines up to 10% of the Company's annual worldwide net sales, and the order would apply immediately during any appeal unless a stay is granted.

answers.reference_answer: Apple says substantially all of its manufacturing is performed in whole or in part by outsourcing partners located primarily in China mainland, India, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and Vietnam, with a significant concentration at a small number of partners, often in single locations. Because it obtains certain components from single or limited sources, Apple is subject to significant supply and pricing risks.

Outsourcing reduces Apple's direct control over production and distribution.

answers.question: Describe the preterm infant formula (NEC) litigation Abbott disclosed in its 2023 10-K.
answers.reference_answer: Abbott is a party to lawsuits alleging that preterm infants developed necrotizing enterocolitis after being given a cow's milk-based preterm infant formula product, resulting in personal injuries or death. In April 2022 the federal cases were consolidated for pretrial purposes in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Illinois.

answers.question: Why did Amazon report a large other expense in 2022, and how does it account for its Rivian investment?
answers.reference_answer: Other income (expense), net swung from $14.6 billion of income in 2021 to $(16.8) billion in 2022, driven largely by a $(12.7) billion valuation loss on Amazon's equity investment in Rivian (after an $11.8 billion gain in 2021). Amazon held about 17% of Rivian's Class A stock, judged it had significant influence (through the investment, its EV purchase arrangement and a board seat), and elected the fair value option, carrying the stake in marketable securities so price changes flow through other income (expense).

Rivian fair value changes are recorded in other income (expense), net.

answers.question: How did Broadcom acquire VMware and what is its strategy for the VMware business, per its fiscal 2024 10-K?
answers.reference_answer: Broadcom completed the VMware merger on November 22, 2023 in a cash-and-stock deal: about $30.8 billion in cash and 544 million Broadcom shares worth $53.4 billion, with the cash funded by $30.4 billion of term loans and cash on hand. answers.question: How does Constellation describe the IRA nuclear production tax credit and its expected effect on its nuclear fleet (2023 10-K)?
answers.reference_answer: The Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 created a nuclear production tax credit of up to $15 per MWh, subject to phase-out, from 2024 through 2032, adjusted annually for inflation. Starting in 2024 Constellation's nuclear fleet is eligible for units not already receiving state support. The credit provides increasing support as unit revenues fall below IRA thresholds, making it an important tool for managing commodity price risk. With this support, Constellation expects its nuclear assets to operate through the end of the credit period.

answers.question: How does Costco value its merchandise inventories, according to its fiscal 2024 10-K?
answers.reference_answer: U.S. merchandise inventories are valued by the cost method on a LIFO basis, which Costco believes more fairly presents results by more closely matching current costs with current revenues. It records an adjustment each quarter, if necessary, for the projected annual effect of inflation or deflation, and adjusts these estimates to actual results at year-end. An immaterial LIFO benefit was recorded in 2024, after an immaterial charge in 2023. Canadian and Other International merchandise inventories are valued mainly with the cost and retail inventory methods, respectively, on a FIFO basis.

Canadian and Other International inventories use FIFO.

answers.question: What is Intel's 2024 Restructuring Plan and what does it involve?
answers.reference_answer: In 2024 Intel announced a series of cost and capital reduction initiatives, called the 2024 Restructuring Plan, designed to adjust its spending to current business trends while enabling its new operating model and continuing to fund its core strategy of returning to product and process competitiveness. It includes cutting headcount (about a 15% reduction in the core Intel workforce by early 2025), consolidating and shrinking its real estate footprint, 'clean sheet' portfolio reviews, rationalizing capital investments by demand and capacity needs, and reducing operating expenses. Intel recognized $2.8 billion of restructuring charges in 2024.

answers.question: Why did Intel record a valuation allowance against its U.S. deferred tax assets in 2024?
answers.reference_answer: Intel assesses the recoverability of its deferred tax assets quarterly, weighing positive and negative evidence. In the third quarter of 2024 it concluded it was more likely than not that its U.S. federal deferred tax assets would not be recovered, because of its three-year cumulative historical loss position, which resulted largely from the asset impairment, restructuring and other charges taken in that quarter. The resulting valuation allowance drove a higher 2024 effective tax rate and about $9.9 billion of non-cash charges to the tax provision.

answers.question: Summarize Coca-Cola's dispute with the IRS over transfer pricing as described in its 2023 10-K, including where the litigation stands and how the company has reserved for it.
answers.reference_answer: In September 2015 the IRS issued a Notice of Deficiency seeking about $3.3 billion of additional federal income tax for 2007-2009, stating its intent to reallocate over $9 billion of income to the U.S. parent company from foreign affiliates it licensed to make and sell its products outside the U.S. The Tax Court's November 2020 opinion predominantly sided with the IRS, while agreeing that dividends previously paid by the foreign licensees could continue to offset royalties, and a November 2023 supplemental opinion also sided with the IRS on the blocked-income regulations. Coca-Cola's conclusion that it is more likely than not its tax positions will ultimately be sustained on appeal is unchanged, and it updated its tax reserve to $439 million as of December 31, 2023.
key_points: The IRS sought about $3.3 billion of additional tax for 2007-2009, reallocating over $9 billion of income to the U.S. parent from licensed foreign affiliates.
The Tax Court's 2020 opinion predominantly sided with the IRS.
A November 2023 supplemental opinion also sided with the IRS (blocked-income regulations).
The company believes it is more likely than not that its tax positions will ultimately be sustained on appeal.
The tax reserve was updated to $439 million as of December 31, 2023.

claims.text: Coca-Cola's 2023 10-K describes an IRS transfer-pricing dispute for 2007-2009 in which the IRS sought about $3.3 billion of additional federal income tax and proposed reallocating over $9 billion of income to the U.S. parent; after the IRS designated the matter for litigation in October 2015, Coca-Cola petitioned the U.S. Tax Court in December 2015, and the Tax Court predominantly sided with the IRS in its November 18, 2020 opinion and again sided with the IRS in a November 8, 2023 supplemental opinion on the blocked-income regulations and 3M precedent, which the company strongly disagrees with and intends to vigorously defend. As of December 31, 2023, the gross amount of unrecognized tax benefits was $929 million, with a net benefit of $632 million if the company prevailed on all uncertain tax positions and $297 million primarily representing tax benefits in different jurisdictions if it did not.

answers.question: Why does Lockheed Martin consider fixed-price development contracts risky, and how does it account for an expected loss on a contract (2023 10-K)?
answers.reference_answer: Lockheed Martin says fixed-price development work or fixed-price production options, especially on competitively bid programs, is inherently riskier than cost-reimbursable work because revenue is fixed while the estimated costs to complete development programs are subject to significant variability. The technical complexity of such programs combined with a fixed-price structure raises the risk that costs exceed expectations, resulting in reduced margins, operating profit or reach-forward losses. When estimated total contract costs exceed the estimated transaction price, it records a provision for the entire loss at the contract level in the period the loss becomes evident, which it calls a reach-forward loss.
key_points: Fixed-price development is riskier because revenue is fixed while costs to complete are highly uncertain.
Technical complexity under a fixed price can lead to reduced margins, operating profit or reach-forward losses.
A reach-forward loss is recorded in full, at the contract level, in the period the loss becomes evident.

claims.text: Lockheed Martin considers fixed-price development contracts risky because revenue is fixed while development costs are highly uncertain due to technical complexity, so cost overruns can reduce margins or produce reach-forward losses; under firm fixed-price contracts it bears cost overruns. For an expected loss, when estimated total contract costs exceed estimated total transaction price, it records a provision for the entire contract-level loss in the period the loss becomes evident.

answers.question: Why does McDonald's emphasize franchising, and how much of its system was franchised at the end of 2025?
answers.reference_answer: About 95% of McDonald's 45,356 restaurants were franchised at year-end 2025. McDonald's says it is primarily a franchisor and believes franchising is paramount to delivering great-tasting food, locally relevant customer experiences and driving profitability: franchising lets an individual be their own employer and control employment, marketing and pricing decisions while benefiting from McDonald's global brand, operating system and financial resources.
key_points: About 95% of 45,356 restaurants were franchised at year-end 2025.
Franchising is seen as paramount to great food, locally relevant experiences and profitability.
Franchisees control employment, marketing and pricing while using the brand and system.

claims.text: McDonald's emphasizes franchising because its heavily franchised business model is designed to generate stable and predictable revenue largely tied to franchisee sales and resulting cash flow, and the Company believes franchising is paramount to delivering great-tasting food, locally relevant customer experiences and driving profitability. At December 31, 2025, approximately 95% of its restaurants worldwide (about 95% of 45,356 restaurants) were franchised.

answers.question: What does Meta's 2024 10-K say about Reality Labs' losses and its outlook for them?
answers.reference_answer: Meta says its significant investments in Reality Labs have generated only limited revenue and reduced its operating margin and profitability, and it expects the adverse impact to continue for the foreseeable future. Reality Labs reduced 2024 operating profit by about $17.73 billion; its loss from operations rose $1.61 billion (10%) from 2023, mainly because of higher employee compensation and infrastructure costs. Meta expects Reality Labs investments and operating losses to increase in 2025.

answers.question: What risks does Merck's 2025 10-K identify around its dependence on Keytruda?
answers.reference_answer: Keytruda represented 49% of Merck's total sales in 2025, so events affecting it could significantly hurt results. Merck expects Keytruda sales to be materially hurt by biosimilar competition between 2028 and 2029; two further patents in the compound patent family run to 2029 through patent term adjustment, but Merck expects them to be litigated. Merck also expects Keytruda to be selected in 2027 for government price setting, effective January 1, 2029, after which it expects U.S. Keytruda sales to decline materially.
key_points: Keytruda was 49% of Merck's total 2025 sales.
Merck expects biosimilar competition to materially hurt Keytruda sales between 2028 and 2029.

answers.question: What change in accounting estimate did Microsoft make for its server and network equipment in fiscal 2023, why, and what was its effect?
answers.reference_answer: Microsoft extended the estimated useful lives of its server and network equipment from four to six years, citing investments in software that made operating that equipment more efficient, and advances in technology. The change in accounting estimate took effect beginning in fiscal 2023 and increased fiscal 2023 operating income by $3.7 billion and net income by $3.0 billion ($0.40 per share); depreciation expense declined in fiscal 2023 as a result.
key_points: Useful lives of server and network equipment were extended from four to six years.

answers.question: How does Netflix amortize its content assets, per its 2023 10-K?
answers.reference_answer: Netflix amortizes licensed and produced content in cost of revenues, based on historical and estimated viewing patterns, over the shorter of each title's contractual window, its estimated period of use, or ten years, starting in the month of first availability. Amortization is accelerated because more viewing is expected up front, and film amortization is more accelerated than TV series. On average over 90% of a licensed or produced content asset is expected to be amortized within four years after first availability.
key_points: Content is amortized based on historical and estimated viewing patterns, over the shorter of the window, estimated use, or ten years.
Amortization is on an accelerated basis, more so for film than TV series.

answers.question: How have U.S. export controls affected NVIDIA's business according to its fiscal 2025 10-K?
answers.reference_answer: NVIDIA says that over the past three years it has been subject to a series of shifting and expanding U.S. export control restrictions that affect its ability to serve customers outside the United States, and it had not received licenses to ship the restricted products to China. Its Data Center revenue in China grew in fiscal 2025 but, as a share of total Data Center revenue, remains well below the levels seen before export controls began in October 2023.

answers.question: What does Oracle's fiscal 2024 10-K say about the risks and expected costs of expanding its data center capacity for Oracle Cloud?
answers.reference_answer: If Oracle cannot secure data center capacity at affordable rates or does not accurately plan its infrastructure capacity, its profitability may decline. It has entered, and expects to keep entering, long-term operating leases with third-party data center providers that generally require significant fees to exit early. Data centers in the geographies it relies on may be unavailable on commercially reasonable terms or at all, and Oracle does not control the operation of these third-party data centers, which may suffer service interruptions from events beyond its control. Oracle expects its cloud services and license support expenses to keep growing in fiscal 2025 as it increases data center capacity and establishes data centers in new geographic locations.
key_points: Inability to secure affordable data center capacity or poor capacity planning could reduce profitability.
Long-term leases with third-party data center providers carry significant early-termination fees.

answers.question: What customer-concentration and vertical-integration risks does Qualcomm describe in its fiscal 2024 10-K, particularly regarding Apple?

answers.question: What are Tesla's automotive regulatory credits and how are they recognized (2022 10-K)?
answers.reference_answer: Tesla earns tradable credits under regulations on zero-emission vehicles, greenhouse gas, fuel economy and clean fuel, and sells them to other regulated entities who use them to meet emission standards. Sales are recognized in automotive regulatory credits revenue. This revenue is tied to Tesla's new vehicle production, sales and negotiated pricing; Tesla monetizes credits proactively as new vehicles are sold under standing arrangements with buyers, typically close to production and delivery or to regulatory changes affecting the credits.
key_points: Tesla earns tradable credits under ZEV, greenhouse gas, fuel economy and clean fuel regulations and sells them to other regulated entities.
Sales are recognized as automotive regulatory credits revenue.
Credits are monetized as vehicles are sold under standing arrangements, so the revenue follows vehicle production and sales.

Automotive regulatory credits revenue increased $311 million, or 21%, in 2022 versus 2021, primarily due to a $288 million regulatory change in Q1 2022 entitling Tesla to additional consideration for credits sold previously.

answers.question: What does TSMC's 2024 annual report say about its Arizona expansion and U.S. CHIPS Act support?

answers.question: How does Texas Instruments describe its capital allocation approach and its outlook for capital expenditures in its 2023 10-K?
answers.reference_answer: Disciplined allocation of capital is the second element of TI's strategy to maximize free cash flow per share growth; it spans how TI selects R&D projects, develops new capabilities, invests in manufacturing capacity, approaches acquisitions and returns cash to its owners. From 2014 to 2023 it allocated $94 billion, the largest share to organic growth (R&D, sales and marketing, capital expenditures and working capital for inventory). It expects capital expenditures to stay higher than historical levels as it invests in manufacturing and technology as part of long-term capacity planning. The U.S. CHIPS and Science Act of August 2022 established a 25% investment tax credit for certain U.S. semiconductor manufacturing investments; TI expects to receive the cash benefit of that credit for qualifying capital expenditures and has applied for the Act's manufacturing grants.

answers.question: How did Union Pacific use its operating cash in 2024, and what capital plan does it describe for 2025?

answers.question: What does UPS's 2024 10-K say about its agreement with Amazon and the network changes it plans in response?
answers.reference_answer: Amazon accounted for 11.8% of UPS's 2024 consolidated revenues. In the first quarter of 2025 UPS reached an agreement in principle with Amazon that will reduce Amazon's volume by more than 50% by June 2026, and UPS is making business and operational changes to match its workforce to its activity and eliminate stranded costs; if it cannot reduce costs, its profitability could be materially impacted. A U.S. network reconfiguration, an expansion of its Network of the Future program, could close up to 10% of its buildings in 2025 and shrink its vehicle and aircraft fleets and workforce; UPS cannot yet estimate the total cost. It expects to partly offset those costs through Efficiency Reimagined initiatives, an end-to-end process redesign expected to yield about $1.0 billion in annualized savings starting in 2025.

answers.question: What did Apple disclose in its fiscal 2024 10-K about the European Commission's Digital Markets Act investigations, and what could the Commission do if it finds a violation?
answers.reference_answer: On March 25, 2024 the Commission opened two formal noncompliance investigations under the DMA: one under Article 5(4) on how developers may communicate and promote offers to users of App Store apps and conclude contracts with them, and one under Article 6(3) on default settings, uninstalling apps and a browser choice screen on iOS. On June 24, 2024 it issued preliminary findings that Apple's App Store rules breach the DMA and opened a third investigation into Apple's new contractual requirements for third-party developers and app marketplaces. If the Commission finds a violation it can issue a cease and desist order and impose fines of up to 10% of Apple's annual worldwide net sales, and its order would apply immediately during an appeal unless stayed. Apple says it believes it complies with the DMA.

Preliminary findings in June 2024 said the App Store rules breach the DMA, and a third investigation into new contractual requirements was opened.

In April 2022 the federal cases were consolidated for pretrial purposes in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Illinois.

answers.question: How does Texas Instruments describe its capital allocation approach and its outlook for capital expenditures in its 2023 10-K?

answers.question: What does UPS's 2024 10-K say about its agreement with Amazon and the network changes it plans in response?
answers.reference_answer: Amazon accounted for 11.8% of UPS's 2024 consolidated revenues. In the first quarter of 2025 UPS reached an agreement in principle with Amazon that will reduce Amazon's volume by more than 50% by June 2026, and UPS is making business and operational changes to match its workforce to its activity and eliminate stranded costs; if it cannot reduce costs, its profitability could be materially impacted. A U.S. network reconfiguration, an expansion of its Network of the Future program, could close up to 10% of its buildings in 2025 and shrink its vehicle and aircraft fleets and workforce; UPS cannot yet estimate the total cost. It expects to partly offset those costs through Efficiency Reimagined initiatives, an end-to-end process redesign expected to yield about $1.0 billion in annualized savings starting in 2025.
key_points: Amazon was 11.8% of UPS's 2024 consolidated revenues.
Under an agreement in principle, Amazon's volume will fall by more than 50% by June 2026.
UPS is matching its workforce to activity and eliminating stranded costs; failure to cut costs could materially hurt profitability.
A U.S. network reconfiguration may close up to 10% of buildings in 2025, and its total cost cannot yet be estimated.
Efficiency Reimagined is expected to save about $1.0 billion a year, starting in 2025, partly offsetting the reconfiguration costs.

answers.question: What drove the changes in Walmart's gross profit rate and operating expense rate in fiscal 2025?
answers.reference_answer: Walmart's gross profit rate rose 40 basis points in fiscal 2025, mainly from the Walmart U.S. segment managing prices in line with its competitive price gaps and from growth in higher-margin businesses globally, partly offset by a mix shift into lower-margin merchandise categories. Operating expenses as a percentage of net sales rose 36 basis points, mainly from higher variable pay after exceeding planned performance, more marketing and higher depreciation.
key_points: Gross profit rate improved because of Walmart U.S. price management and growth in higher-margin businesses.
A mix shift into lower-margin merchandise partly offset the gross margin gain.
The operating expense rate rose because of higher variable pay, marketing and depreciation.
